transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well... what brings me in is that I keep getting hit out of nowhere with the scene of my cousin on that pavement. It's... it's like I can actually hear the shouting and see the lights all over again. It just happens even when I'm standing in the church office, you know, just trying to act normal and do my job.
When did this event with your cousin happen?
It happened two years and three months ago. That's... that's when he was killed. And this has just been going on ever since then.
Do you find yourself going out of your way to avoid reminders, thoughts, or places connected to what happened to your cousin?

Yeah, I do. I actually take the long way around town now just so I don't have to pass by the community center or that court. I just can't look at it. And... if someone brings up that night, or even starts talking about it, I just shut the conversation down immediately. Or I'll just find some excuse to leave the room. I just can't be around it.
Have you found yourself feeling constantly on edge, watchful, or on guard since that happened?

Yes, absolutely. I... I can't even sit with my back to a door anymore. It's just impossible. And when I'm at church events, instead of paying attention to the people standing right in front of me, I'm always watching their hands, or checking the corners of the room. I'll catch myself watching cars slowing down outside, and I always have to know exactly where the nearest exit is. I'm just constantly scanning everything.

inference_history.note: Initial differential based on intrusive re-experiencing/flashbacks of a traumatic event involving the patient's cousin.
Ruled out F43.0 because the event occurred over two years ago, far exceeding the timeframe for an acute stress reaction.
Ruled out F43.2 due to presence of classic intrusive re-experiencing and active avoidance symptoms specific to traumatic bereavement lasting over two years.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experienced a severe traumatic event (witnessing the violent death of their cousin) over two years ago and presents with classic persistent symptoms of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, including vivid intrusive re-experiencing/flashbacks, active avoidance of trauma-related triggers and conversations, and marked hyperarousal and hypervigilance.

confirmed_symptoms: Recurrent, intrusive distressing memories and flashbacks where the patient relives the scene with sights and sounds of the traumatic event
Active avoidance of geographical reminders and locations associated with the event (taking alternative routes around town)
Avoidance of external reminders, conversations, or discussions about the trauma
Persistent hypervigilance (scanning room corners, monitoring exits, watching people's hands and passing cars)
Marked feeling of being on edge and unable to sit with back to doors

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have been persistent for 2 years and 3 months following the trauma.
additional_requirements: Exposure to a traumatic stressor involving catastrophic/violent death of a family member
